newsitem.title: UK: Barclays shrugs off buyback tax ruling.
newsitem.headline: Barclays shrugs off buyback tax ruling.

text.p: Barclays Plc on Tuesday shrugged off a British Treasury move to close a tax loophole on share buybacks and said it would make no difference to its policy towards repurchasing its own shares.

A spokeswoman for Barclays said the company had already carried out three share repurchases and today's Treasury ruling would not affect any plans it might have to use further buybacks as part of the management of its capital.
"We will continue to use the purchases of our own shares as a mechanism for managing the equity element of our capital," the spokeswoman said.
The Treasury statement "doesn't change our plans", the spokeswoman said.

Earlier a statement from Chancellor Kenneth Clarke cancelled special tax credits for pension funds on share buybacks and some types of special dividends, popular among cash-rich UK banks in recent months as a means of using up surplus capital.

Yet some market sources said they had expected the closure of the loophole on share buybacks -- which meant pension funds could reclaim 25 percent tax on the difference between a share repurchase price and the stock's original issue price.
"It was not a great surprise," said one source.
Barclays shares were down 8-1/2p at 966 by 1446 GMT, after rallying from a decline as low as 947p immediately after the Treasury statement.
